newsitem.title: USA: Jury seated in N.C. racial murder trial.
newsitem.headline: Jury seated in N.C. racial murder trial.

text.p: A jury was seated Wednesday for the trial of a white former U.S. army paratrooper charged in the 1995 racially motivated slayings of two black Fayetteville, N.C., residents.
It took lawyers more than two weeks to pick the 12-member jury of six white women, five white men and one black woman.

The panel will hear evidence against Malcolm Wright in New Hanover County Superior Court, where the trial was moved because of pretrial publicity stemming from the trial of James Burmeister, another former paratrooper who was convicted of murder on Feb. 27 in Fayetteville.
Opening arguments were scheduled to begin later Wednesday.

Wright, 22, faced two counts of first degree murder and one count of conspiracy to commit first-degree murder in the deaths of Michael James, 36, and Jackie Burden, 27, who were gunned down on a Fayetteville street on Dec. 7, 1995.
Prosecutors said they would seek the death penalty.
Judge Coy Brewer, who presided over the Burmeister trial, last month denied a series of defence motions that would have prevented the death penalty from being considered in Wright's case.

His lawyers had argued that it would be "fundamentally unfair" for Wright to face the death penalty since a third soldier charged in the crime, Randy Meadows, testified that Burmeister admitted to shooting James and Burden.

Meadows, 22, served as the state's key witness in the Burmeister trial and also will testify against Wright. Burmeister, 21, a one-time member of Fort Bragg's elite 82nd Airborne Division, is serving two consecutive life sentences after a jury deadlocked 11-1 in favour of executing him.
